chunks.title: Light, refraction & critical angle
chunks.tldr: Speed = frequency × wavelength; in media speed and wavelength change, frequency (colour) doesn't. Refractive index n = c(vacuum)/c(medium): air ~1.0003, water/aqueous ~1.33–1.34, PMMA 1.49, crown glass 1.52, flint 1.62, silicone 1.44. n rises with temperature (plastic/aqueous ~150× glass). Dispersion: n higher for blue; Abbe value V high = less dispersion. Snell: n sin i = n' sin i'. Reflection: angle in = angle out. Fermat: least-time path; optical path = n × distance. Denser → rarer medium: beyond the critical angle → total internal reflection (fibre-optics). Aqueous critical angle ~48° → angle structures invisible without a gonio lens.
chunks.hook: You need a goniolens because the angle's light is trapped by total internal reflection.

cards.q: Why can't the iridocorneal angle be seen directly?
cards.a: Light from the angle exceeds the critical angle (~46–48°) at the cornea/tear–air interface and is totally internally reflected; a goniolens eliminates the air interface.

cards.q: What stays constant when light enters a new medium?
cards.a: Frequency (and hence colour); speed and wavelength change.

chunks.title: Lens formulas, vertex distance & aberrations
chunks.tldr: Thin-lens algebra (approximate): Power (D) = 1/f (m); 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; magnification = image/object size = image/object distance; powers add for thin, close lenses. Thick lenses need two principal planes and nodal points; back vertex power is what the lensmeter reads. Trigonometric ray-tracing is exact (needed for IOLs, CLs, refractive surgery). Contact lens power ≈ 0.34/r. Vertex distance: P₂ = 1/(1/P₁ − d) — moving a plus lens closer needs more plus (+13 D at 11 mm → +15.2 D contact lens); minus lens closer needs less minus. Aberrations: chromatic (blue focuses in front), spherical (periphery bends more), coma, oblique astigmatism, curvature of field, distortion (pincushion/barrel); reduced by meniscus/aspheric design, stops, achromatic doublets.
chunks.hook: Plus lens forward = stronger. Hyperope's contact lens needs more plus than their specs.

cards.q: A +13 D spectacle at 11 mm; approximate contact lens power?

chunks.title: Cylinders, Sturm's conoid & prisms
chunks.tldr: Planocylinder: no power along its axis, max power 90° away → line focus parallel to axis. Spherocylinder → conoid of Sturm: two focal lines (interval of Sturm), circle of least confusion between. Transposition: add sphere + cylinder, flip cylinder sign, rotate axis 90° (+2.00/−3.00×90 = −1.00/+3.00×180). Prism: light bends toward base, image displaced toward apex; 1 PD = 1 cm at 1 m (~0.57°; 2 PD ≈ 1°). Glass prisms calibrated in Prentice position, plastic in minimum deviation. Prentice's rule: prism (PD) = decentration (cm) × power (D); plus lens base toward centre, minus base away. Anisometropia → vertical prism when reading → chin-down, slab-off, or CLs. Fresnel press-on prisms: light but scatter. Hand neutralisation: minus = 'with' movement, plus = against; cylinder = scissor/rotation distortion.
chunks.hook: Prism: light to the Base, image to the Apex.

cards.q: Prism induced 5 mm from the centre of a +6 D lens?
cards.a: 3 prism dioptres (Prentice: 0.5 cm × 6 D), base toward the optical centre.

chunks.title: Optics of the eye & visual acuity
chunks.tldr: Classic simplification: cornea ~43 D, lens ~19 D, total ~60 D; reduced schematic eye (Gullstrand): single surface, n 1.33, axial length 22.5 mm — mathematical convenience, not physiology. Vaughan: better viewed as a three-lens system (aqueous, crystalline lens with graded index, vitreous); the cornea mostly shapes the aqueous lens. Accommodation from lens change (Purkinje images). Resolution ~1 arc-minute; Snellen letter 5×5 units → 6/6 letter subtends 5′ (8.7 mm at 6 m, ~0.025 mm on retina ≈ 100 lines/mm).
chunks.hook: 6/6 letter = 5 minutes of arc; each stroke = 1 minute.

cards.q: What angle does a 6/6 Snellen letter subtend?

chunks.title: Presbyopia, myopia & hyperopia
chunks.tldr: Accommodation falls: ~14 D at 8, 10 D at 25, 6 D at 40, 2 D at 50, ~1 D at 55 → presbyopia noticed ~44–46 (worse in dim light), stable ~55; reading glasses, bifocals, trifocals, varifocals. Myopia: image in front; axial (~3 D per extra mm) or refractive; far point = 1/D (far point 25 cm → −4 D); can read unaided when presbyopic; high myopia → RD, degeneration; concave lens. Hyperopia: image behind; short eye or low power (aphakia); young compensate by accommodating (latent) — cycloplegia reveals total; manifest = not overcome; causes asthenopia, esotropia, amblyopia; presbyopia arrives earlier, then blur at all distances.
chunks.hook: Myope's far point in metres = 1 / dioptres of myopia.

cards.q: Each extra millimetre of axial length adds about how much myopia?

cards.a: The part of hyperopia masked by accommodation, revealed only with cycloplegia.

chunks.title: Astigmatism, development & anisometropia
chunks.tldr: Regular astigmatism: two principal meridians 90° apart → compound/simple myopic, mixed, simple/compound hyperopic. With-the-rule (vertical meridian steeper; correct with minus cyl at 180, plus cyl at 90) — young. Against-the-rule (horizontal steeper) — elderly. Oblique if axes >20° off. Irregular (keratoconus, scars) → rigid CL. Lenticular = 'residual' astigmatism (not fixed by spherical RGP). New cyl correction → temporary tilt/distortion. Development: newborn ~+0.5 D, cornea 6.59 → 7.71 mm radius by 1 y, axial length 16.6 mm → 21.8 mm (2–3 y) → 24 mm by 10–15 y; myopia rises in teens (near work); progression treatments then unproven. Anisometropia: amblyopia (more hyperopic eye), aniseikonia — monocular aphakia: specs ~25% image difference (intolerable), CL ~6%, IOL <1%.

cards.q: Image size difference in monocular aphakia with spectacles vs CL vs IOL?
Which meridian is steeper in with-the-rule astigmatism?

chunks.title: Spectacles, contact lenses & IOL formulas
chunks.tldr: Spectacles: safest; meniscus form, pantoscopic tilt. Rigid (PMMA → RGP): tear lens neutralises corneal (incl. irregular) astigmatism; power = base-curve effect + lens power. Soft drape onto cornea → need toric for astigmatism; base curve from keratometry; risk of keratitis. Uses: keratoconus (RGP), bandage (soft), aphakia, high myopia (better image than specs); mostly cosmetic. IOLs: in-the-bag foldable acrylic/silicone; power from biometry: SRK: P = A − 2.5L − 0.9K (regression, old); modern theoretical: Hoffer Q (short <22 mm), Holladay (24.6–26 mm), Haigis/SRK-T (>26 mm). Post-refractive-surgery eyes → underestimated power unless pre-op data. Piggyback IOL, phakic IOL, clear lens extraction (high myopes — RD risk).
chunks.hook: Short eye = Hoffer Q; long eye = SRK/T.

cards.a: IOL power = A − 2.5 × axial length (mm) − 0.9 × average K.

cards.q: IOL formula preferred for short eyes (<22 mm)?

chunks.title: Retinoscopy & subjective refraction
chunks.tldr: Retinoscopy: streak (intercept) → pupillary reflex; aligned reflex = sphere or on-axis cylinder; rotate streak to find meridians. 'With' movement → add plus; 'against' → add minus; neutral = whole pupil fills, no movement. Then subtract working distance: 1/distance — at 2/3 m subtract 1.50 D (at 50 cm subtract 2.00 D). Autorefractors unreliable in kids/opaque media. Subjective: maximum plus for best acuity (fight accommodation); duochrome — equal red/green = done (red clearer → add minus; green clearer → add plus); Jackson cross cylinder (±cyl with sphere half opposite) to refine axis then power. Cycloplegic: fogging in adults; children cyclopentolate 1%, or atropine 0.5–1% ointment bd ×3 days for dark irides/accommodative ET.
chunks.hook: WITH = Wants plus; against = add minus. Then take off 1.50.

cards.q: Retinoscopy at 66 cm neutralises with +3.50 D. Refraction?
On the duochrome test, letters are clearer on red. What next?
cards.a: Add minus (the patient is relatively myopic/over-plussed).
